title: Even exact graph-cycle Berry data leave the two-dimensional Chern number undetermined
statement: Smooth gapped two-band Hamiltonians can agree on an open neighborhood of any finite embedded graph in T^2 while their lower-band Chern numbers differ by any integer, if one such extension exists.

requires: A finite embedded1-skeleton, an unused disjoint disk and an existing smooth gapped two-band extension.
provides: Smooth gapped two-band Hamiltonians can agree on an open neighborhood of any finite embedded graph in T^2 while their lower-band Chern numbers differ by any integer, if one such extension exists.
assumptions: Graph-cycle holonomy is not a two-dimensional occupied-projector/curvature field. A valid extra face-extension rule could remove this ambiguity; none is supplied by the inspected finite data.
costs: A smooth gapped face extension/projector field and its observable coupling are extra structure. Finite graph-cycle data alone do not supply them.
contract.units: The Chern number is an integer with declared orientation/band convention; periodic coordinates and the nonzero band gap belong to the actual two-parameter model.
contract.obstruction: Provide and justify the missing two-dimensional gapped extension and its transport observable; equal graph holonomies do not fix the Chern integer.

body: Spectrally flatten to n(k).sigma. Flatten n to a constant on a disk disjoint from the graph without changing its degree or graph data, then insert a smooth degree-j sphere bubble with a constant collar. The resulting unit-vector map preserves the gap and all graph-neighborhood projectors/holonomies while shifting the Chern integer byj. The two explicit benchmark models already agree on ky=0 but have Chern0and magnitude1. Numerical grids are diagnostic; the supported smooth construction proves the underdetermination.
